meaning: The number 60 symbolizes completeness, abundance, and wealth in biblical and Jewish tradition.
description: In Song of Songs 6:8, sixty queens are mentioned as part of an image of royal richness and abundance. The number 60 has deep roots in ancient culture through the sexagesimal numeral system, which also influenced biblical measures and timekeeping. In the courtyard of the Tabernacle, the total number of pillars can be calculated as 60, linking the number to the structure of the sanctuary. In Jewish tradition, 60 is associated with completeness, and the Talmud uses one-sixtieth as an important threshold value in several areas.

versions.meaning: The number 60 symbolizes completeness, abundance, and maturity in biblical and Jewish tradition.
versions.description: In Song of Songs 6:8, sixty queens are mentioned as part of an image of wealth and abundance. In Jewish tradition, 60 is associated with completeness, including through Talmudic references where 1/60 serves as a threshold for nullifying mixtures (bitul b'shishim), and it is said that sleep is one-sixth of death. The number also appears in connection with the Mishkan (tabernacle), where certain measurements and the number of support pillars were 60.

footnotes.text: The sexagesimal numeral system (base-60) originates from ancient Mesopotamia (Sumer and Babylon) and forms the basis for our division of hours into 60 minutes and minutes into 60 seconds. The system also influenced biblical weights and measures.
In the courtyard of the Mishkan (Tabernacle), the total number of pillars can be calculated as 60 by summing the pillars on all four sides (20+20+10+10), based on Exodus 27:9–18.

The principle bitul b'shishim (nullification in one-sixtieth) is an important halachic rule in the Talmud (Chulin 98b): if a forbidden substance makes up less than 1/60 of a mixture, it is considered nullified. The number 60 thus serves as a threshold for complete dissolution.

In the Talmud (Berachot 57b), it is said that sleep is one-sixtieth of death, fire one-sixtieth of Gehinnom, and honey one-sixtieth of manna – all expressions showing that 60 represents a complete whole containing a faint reflection of something greater.
